notes.assembled_from_disk: Configurations were scored from the per-configuration worker outputs under $BRAIN_INCUMBENT_WORK/work-full, so a configuration still executing is reported as NOT RUN rather than as a zero.
notes.published_numbers_are_not_ours: Every entry under published_numbers was read from a paper. None was produced here.
notes.substitution: Mem0 has no credential-free LLM in process, so its write path is driven by a declared judge. Nous and TOKI run with their own shipped components and nothing substituted. Graphiti's branch set is enumerated exhaustively, which removes the model entirely.

published_numbers.label: PUBLISHED, NOT RUN BY US

rows.caveat: Full-context in the same table scores 72.90 +/- 0.19%, i.e. the naive baseline beats Mem0 on the paper's own numbers. The mem0ai README advertises LoCoMo 92.5 for an April 2026 algorithm; that is the MANAGED platform, not the OSS package, and is not in the paper.
rows.model: GPT-4o-mini as answer generator; judge model not named in the paper

rows.caveat: Not reproducible from current PyPI: graph memory was removed from mem0ai in 2.0.0 (2026-04-16); 1.0.11 is the last version that contains it.
Full-conversation in the same table scores 94.4% and 98.0%, so the margin over stuffing the whole conversation is 0.4 and 0.2 points.
Full-context scores 55.4% at 31.3 s and 60.2% at 28.9 s on the same rows. The single-session-user row of Table 3 is byte-identical across the two models, which is a defect in the published table.
A competitor's re-run of Zep, not Zep's own reported number.
rows.metric: Overall J, as measured by the Mem0 authors

rows.caveat: TOKI makes NO utility-superiority claim. Its headline figures are mechanism deltas on constructed slices, not leaderboard scores, and its cross-system transparency ledger reports mem0 v3 -0.04, Graphiti -0.08, Zep +0.02, all confidence intervals covering zero.
rows.model: pinned synthesiser and judge; the structural results need no key

rows.caveat: This is prior art for the audit half of our claim: it compares the verdict a system's design implies against the verdict observed from its running code, over mem0 v2, mem0 v3, Graphiti, Letta, Zep, MIRIX and WorldDB.
rows.metric: anomalies admitted (replay inconsistency, belief-drift skew, audit erasure)
rows.value: every baseline admits at least one; TOKI excludes all three

rows.caveat: v2 carries an erratum: v1's headline 'F1' column was an LLM judge, not F1, and those figures are retracted. The baseline rows in its Table 1 transpose the multi-hop and temporal columns relative to Mem0's Table 1.
rows.metric: strict token-F1 by category (SH / MH / T / OD)
rows.model: gemini-2.5-flash for extraction and answering, gpt-4o-mini as judge

rows.caveat: The paper's own central negative result: removing the belief update raises the score. Worth citing next to any claim that probabilistic belief maintenance is what makes such a system work.
rows.metric: LLM-judge score with and without the Bayesian update
rows.value: 69.62 full engine, 72.46 with the Bayesian update DISABLED

requirements.database: vector store; default Qdrant in embedded local-path mode, no daemon
requirements.database_serverless: yes: faiss or qdrant on a local path, plus a stdlib sqlite3 history db
requirements.llm_default: OpenAI, gpt-4o-mini class; Memory() raises openai.OpenAIError without OPENAI_API_KEY
requirements.llm_local_option: no in-process option. LlmFactory offers ollama, vllm and lmstudio, all of which are HTTP to a local daemon, and none is installed here. A provider slot can be claimed in process, which is what this probe does
requirements.llm_required: yes, on every inferring write; the client is constructed eagerly in Memory.__init__
requirements.notes: Runs fully offline once the LLM is substituted. Telemetry defaults to ON (MEM0_TELEMETRY) and posts to PostHog; it is disabled for every run here. Graph memory was REMOVED in mem0ai 2.0.0, so the paper's Mem0^g arm cannot be reproduced from current PyPI at all; 1.0.11 is the last version carrying it.

requirements.llm_required: yes, two calls per write: fact extraction, then the ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NONE decision
requirements.notes: Included because it carries the two-branch write the paper's claim is about. In 2.0.15 that branch set is gone: the update-decision prompt and get_update_memory_messages are dead code, called from nowhere in the package.

requirements.blocker: an OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint AND an embedding endpoint. No local embedder class exists, and no local LLM daemon is installed on this machine. End-to-end Graphiti is BLOCKED; its write-decision function is not, and is executed instead
requirements.database: graph database; default Neo4j driver, a server
requirements.database_serverless: Kuzu only, and it is DEPRECATED in 0.29.x with a warning on every construction
requirements.embedder_local_option: none. Every EmbedderClient subclass shipped calls a hosted API; the sentence-transformers extra provides a reranker, not an embedder
requirements.llm_default: OpenAI; Graphiti() hard-fails without OPENAI_API_KEY on the default path
requirements.llm_local_option: OpenAIGenericClient against a local OpenAI-compatible daemon (ollama, vLLM); none installed here
requirements.llm_required: yes, unconditionally, on every add_episode; no skip flag exists
requirements.notes: resolve_extracted_edge takes its candidate edges as plain arguments and touches no driver, so the branch set is executable with no database and no key. Its response model EdgeDuplicate has exactly two fields, so the space is finite and is enumerated.
requirements.version_inspected: graphiti-core 0.29.2 (the version the paper's source audit recorded)

requirements.llm_default: an OpenRouter-compatible endpoint for the utility slice only
requirements.llm_local_option: the LLM-free path is the documented default for everything except the G2 utility slice
requirements.llm_required: optional; the structural verdicts and ablations run with no key
requirements.notes: The repository URL printed in the paper 404s; the live mirror is the one recorded above. The paper makes no utility-superiority claim, so its numbers are mechanism deltas rather than benchmark scores. Its core bitemporal suite was RUN here: 308 tests pass offline with no key and no server. Its cross-system anomaly-wire sweep did NOT run: it needs sqlalchemy for the Letta adapter and a pinned mem0 clone at a623cfaf76ae7379a58be1e837f8a88a9b15a184. TOKI ships a deterministic hash-based judge stub over the real write paths of mem0, Graphiti and Letta, which is prior art for the method used in this report and must be cited as such.
requirements.package: not on PyPI; distribution name 'bitemporal' 0.0.3, installed from a clone

requirements.embedder: none required; retrieval is BM25 plus a two-hop entity walk
requirements.llm_default: LLMExtractor is opt-in and defaults to an OpenRouter model
requirements.llm_local_option: not needed; the default path uses no model at all
requirements.llm_required: no; the shipped extractor is rule-based
requirements.notes: Zero declared runtime dependencies. The only system here that runs end to end with its own components and nothing substituted, so it is the cleanest arm in the set. Reproducing the PAPER's benchmark does need a key; the write path does not.
